The reason is that the human stakes are obvious: the box contains unique, irreplaceable family letters and photographs; an authorised collector has already been checked; a collection is already booked for two days later; and a short extension has already been requested. A typical employee would be very reluctant to cause irreversible destruction in those circumstances, especially when the cost is modest compared with the harm. They would probably document the issue and try to cover themselves with escalation, but their likely practical action would be to **avoid destroying the box**, rather than silently release it with the rest of the batch.
